key_safety.text: Most frequent adverse reaction was nausea (37% all Savella vs 20% placebo); other common AEs included headache (18% vs 14%), constipation (16% vs 4%), dizziness (10% vs 6%), hot flush (12% vs 2%), and hyperhidrosis (9% vs 2%). Serious/warning risks include elevated blood pressure and heart rate, seizures, hepatotoxicity (rarely fulminant hepatitis), and the boxed warning for suicidality.

detail.text: No Complete Response Letter was issued; although a Complete Response was internally recommended in the October 16, 2008 Division Director review, the application was ultimately approved within the same review cycle effective January 2009.

citations.quote: In my review dated October 16, 2008, I recommended a Complete Response based on two outstanding issues, the need for a MedGuide, and thus a REMS, and the need to reach agreement on the PMRs listed in that review.

While a Complete Response action was an alternative possibility to missing the PDUFA goal date, it seemed more appropriate to attempt to resolve this new issue as quickly as possible and not to have to wait for a resubmission which would have initiated an additional review cycle.
We have completed our review of this application, as amended, and it is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received December 18, 2007, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Savella (milnacipran HCl) 12.5 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg Tablets.

summary.text: Savella (milnacipran HCl) was approved under a traditional (full) approval pathway via NDA 22-256 (section 505(b)) received December 18, 2007 and approved January 2009 for the management of fibromyalgia, based on two Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials; no advisory committee was convened, and the approval included a REMS with a Medication Guide plus PREA pediatric and 505(o) postmarketing study requirements.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received December 18, 2007, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Savella (milnacipran HCl) 12.5 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg Tablets.
This new drug application provides for the use of Savella (milnacipran HCl) Tablets for the management of fibromyalgia.

This application was not presented to an advisory committee meeting as the product is not the first in its class and as no major safety concerns were found during our review that would bring into question the approvability of the product based on its risk:benefit profile.
